identity.title: The ALMA Frontier Fields Survey. II. Multiwavelength Photometric analysis of 1.1 mm continuum sources in Abell 2744, MACSJ0416.1-2403 and MACSJ1149.5+2223

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report on the multi-wavelength photometric analysis of all 12 significantly detected (>5σ) sources in the first three Frontier Fields clusters observed by ALMA, based on data from Hubble and Spitzer, the Very Large Telescope and the Herschel Space Observatory.

question.value: What are the optical/NIR/FIR counterparts, photometric redshifts and physical properties (stellar mass, SFR, dust) of the 12 ALMA 1.1 mm >5σ sources in A2744, M0416 and M1149?

evidence.quote: We report here on the photometric analysis of all 1.1 mm continuum detections, combining data from the HST, VLT, Spitzer and Herschel observatories.
The ALMA Frontier Fields survey (ID 2013.1.00999.S, PI: F. Bauer)
was designed to produce deep ≈2.′1×2.′2 maps at 1.1mm covering the HST/WFC3 fields-of-view for all six clusters.

claims.hypothesis: Do the ALMA-FF sources have robust NIR counterparts and are they red?

claims.result: Clear counterparts for all but one source; eight of 11 have F814W-Ks ≳ 4.

evidence.quote: We identify robust near-infrared (NIR) counterparts for all 11 sources with Ks detection

claims.hypothesis: Does the SED-fitting methodology yield reliable photo-z?

claims.result: Mean z=1.99±0.27 and broad agreement with GLASS, though A2744-ID02 is inconsistent from the NIR-SED.

evidence.quote: This verification confirms the validity of our photometric redshift methodology.
